scene-editor.environment: Node VM + minimal DOM harness + native Canvas; not a browser
passed: Editor opens from the title with 330 locally drawn objects and all 17 maps, without creating or overwriting an adventure. Every default map passes continuous-edge reachability checks.
Real palette placement, pointer drag, coordinate inspector, rotated collisions, collision toggles, duplication, removal and undo/redo handlers work together.

Moving a usable bench rebuilds its reserved activity destination. Moving a vendor counter moves its work anchors and resident home; moving a hosted food interaction moves its counter. Campaign NPCs cannot be deleted.
Path painting, custom musical interaction, authored labels and a collision-aware walking preview work through UI handlers. Escape resumes editing; the visit does not advance quests.

Export/import preserves authored scenes and all 17 map profiles, excludes adventure data and rejects unknown assets, invalid coordinates, missing educational interactions and prototype keys. Drafts reopen; applied layouts use separate LocalStorage keys.

F2 opens during play; simulation and play time pause, save writes are suppressed, and visits to locked editor maps leave campaign progress unchanged. Added instruments play normally after application. Blocked layouts are rejected atomically, preserving portals, doors and characters.
Applied editor layouts survive reload and rebuilding alongside version-1 adventure saves; minimap cache keys include layout revisions.
limitations: CSS panel layout and real pointer capture, touch, file picker and browser audio require supported-browser verification.

Optional heritage progress normalizes malformed and earlier saves without losing chapter progress; cultural text remains available with reduced motion and ambient chatter disabled.
limitations: No browser was available. CSS, native pointer capture, touch, file picker and audible Web Audio were not verified.

neighborhood.environment: Node VM + minimal DOM + native Canvas; no browser
passed: All 50 readings keep IDs, sources and connected paragraphs. Grade-specific, scalar, dynamic and branching dialogue translations remain nonempty and resolve correctly for grades 6, 7 and 8.
The 64 new local assets include 12 historical portraits placed in relevant locations. Every portrait opens its corresponding sourced reading; portraits and skin tones have no recoloring roles.

The protest has 24 distinct original participants and 24 physical body bounds, readable signs, fictional neighbor dialogue and a sourced historical panel. Chatter/mute controls and the low bubble limit are respected.
Material changes affect only declared wood/fabric pixels; original outlines, highlights outside those roles and transparency stay intact.

Scale, rotation and declared material colors work through actual inspector handlers on original objects and new furniture; collision geometry scales with the fountain, and duplication preserves furniture colors.
Whole and half rectangular floor tiles paint by pointer stroke, rotate into either axis, preserve colors, undo/redo as one action and cancel without leaving partial paint.

Optional protest and heritage displays can be deleted without lingering collisions or being resurrected by current imports. Essential protections remain active; invalid colors and scales are rejected.

Scale/color/floor edits survive apply and full-world reload using a separate layout save. Older revision-2 scene files gain the new optional exhibits; campaign progress remains byte-equivalent except its save timestamp.
Printed book text and pencil notebook/note text use bundled fonts with local licenses. The 108 educational questions, 20 optional missions and offline asset loading remain available.
limitations: Responsive CSS, actual browser typography, pointer capture/touch and audible Web Audio require a supported browser.
